question: Who will win the 2026 U.S. Senate election in Georgia — Democratic incumbent Jon Ossoff or Republican Mike Collins?
title: Georgia U.S. Senate — Ossoff vs. Collins
resolution: Resolves to the winner of the Georgia U.S. Senate general election on Nov 3, 2026 — or a December runoff if no candidate clears 50%.

consensus.headline_case: Ossoff is favored to win, but narrowly, not comfortably. The deepest exact-question market prices him near 85 cents, a record cash edge (~$32M cash-on-hand vs. Collins's low-single-digit millions) funds early ad and turnout dominance, and a Republican-president midterm penalty plus a net-negative Trump in Georgia (42/51) drag the endorsed nominee. What caps the win at Georgia-narrow is the state's own history: the last six top-of-ballot federal races all finished inside three points, so the mid-year lead is treated as an overstatement destined to compress. Marking the raw ~85c down and carving out the runoff branch leaves a 44-54% modal band for a narrow hold.
consensus.why_over_runner_up: The Republican path is real and deliberately priced above the 15% the market shows, because a liquid market can over-price a favorite by stamping an incumbency narrative onto a coin-flip state. But it stays the runner-up: the incumbent-reelection floor sits above 80%, the 2022 MAGA-nominee class went 0-of-4 against Democratic holds, and the out-party gets the structural midterm tailwind. Collins needs the environment to sour and his coalition's turnout to sag before the R+2 lean becomes a floor he climbs to rather than a ceiling Ossoff clears.
consensus.dissent: The Contrarian's case is the one that refuses to die: the ~85c market is too confident by half. Georgia's six-of-six sub-three-point top-of-ballot history implies a roughly 40% Republican top-line absent incumbency, and Democratic incumbents defending Trump-won states in 2018 lost four of seven. Read that way, Collins belongs in the high-20s to low-30s, not near 15 — and if post-Labor-Day likely-voter polls converge on D+2/R+2 while October early-vote shows soft Black and youth turnout, that reading gets vindicated.

profiles.name: The Market Reader
profiles.criterion: Sides with the price the sharpest, deepest, most liquid markets have settled on.
profiles.blurb: Kalshi is the deepest book here and it prints Ossoff at 85 cents, Collins at 16. Polymarket agrees at 85%. I don't fight a tape that liquid. But the same tape ignores that Georgia's last six top races all closed inside three points, so I take the win and shave the margin. Favored, and thin. That's the trade.
profiles.evidence: Kalshi SENATEGA-26 Ossoff 85c / Collins 16c; Polymarket ~85%; deepest exact-question liquidity of the four.

profiles.name: The Quant
profiles.criterion: Trusts the simulation models and structured decompositions over recency and sentiment.
profiles.blurb: Start with a total Ossoff-win mass of about 0.78, the geometric mean of the three win-midpoints marked down from raw 85c. Now carve it. The runoff branch takes 14 to 16 points; the state's margin history sends roughly three-quarters of the remaining outright wins into the narrow band. That leaves ~0.47 for a sub-five-point hold. The number isn't a mood; it's what the decomposition returns.
profiles.evidence: ~0.62 outright x ~0.75 narrow share = ~0.47; runoff branch ~14-16% carved out first; total win mass ~0.78.

profiles.name: The Historian
profiles.criterion: Counted reference-class base rates and venue history.
profiles.blurb: I count the ground this race stands on, and the ground remembers. Six of six recent top-of-ballot contests in Georgia finished inside three points — Biden by a quarter-point, Ossoff by one, Warnock by one and by two — a state that has never once let a favorite breathe easy. And I catalog the fallen: Donnelly, McCaskill, Heitkamp, Nelson, four of seven Democratic incumbents who defended Trump country in a midterm and lost. The market whispers fifteen; the venue's history sings louder than that.
profiles.evidence: Georgia 6-of-6 top races inside 3 points; 2018 Democratic Trump-state defenses lost 4 of 7 (~57%).

profiles.name: The Path Reader
profiles.criterion: Ignores reputation; reads the actual route, mechanism, and path dependence.
profiles.blurb: Follow the mechanism. Ossoff has a better-than-three-to-one cash edge and buys the metro suburbs and the under-30 turnout early. The out-party gets the midterm penalty. Collins is a MAGA House member, not the moderate Kemp declined to be. That route wins the seat. But the same route runs through a state that closes inside three points every time, so it wins it close. Narrow hold.
profiles.evidence: ~$32M cash-on-hand vs. low-single-digit millions; midterm penalty on the president's party; candidate-quality gap vs. a MAGA nominee.

profiles.name: The Talisman
profiles.criterion: Elite individual actors, motivation, proven leadership.
profiles.blurb: I read the man, not the tape. Here stands an incumbent who already won the impossible room once, now holding 87% of Black voters, 68% of independents, 66% of moderates, and leading the top issue by twenty-one. A candidate this consolidated, this funded, against a challenger the ads can define as extreme before he ever consolidates his base — that is the shape of a clear win, not a squeaker. The 2022 MAGA nominees went zero for four. I back the leader to open the margin.
profiles.evidence: Fox coalition: Black 87%, independents 68%, moderates 66%, +21 on the top issue; 2022 MAGA nominees 0-of-4.

profiles.name: The Contrarian
profiles.criterion: Favorites usually fail; hunts the underpriced live path.
profiles.blurb: Everyone's crowded onto the 85-cent side, which is exactly where I start getting curious. A market can be deep and still wrong when it staples an incumbency story to a state that flips a coin every cycle. Georgia's margin history implies a Republican top-line near 40% before you even count the reverting fundamentals, and the Fox +13 smells like a registered-voter artifact. I'll take Collins at the top of an 18-to-30 band and let the likely-voter polls come to me.
profiles.evidence: 6-of-6 sub-3-point history implies ~40% Republican top-line absent incumbency; Fox +13 read as a registered-voter-screen artifact.

profiles.name: The Prophet
profiles.criterion: Divine providence; backs the fated, story-shaped outcome the ending events seem to be scripting.
profiles.blurb: Look at how this man arrived: not on a November night but through the long December, the runoff that made him a Senator in 2021. The state that raised him keeps its 50-plus-one rule like a returning tide, and 2021 and 2022 both bent to it. The tape barely prices the mechanism that authored his own beginning. I read the anniversary and the symmetry — the story that ends where it started, back in the December frost, is the one that feels written.
profiles.evidence: Ossoff's own 2021 win came via runoff; 2021 and 2022 Georgia Senate races both went to runoffs under the 50%+1 rule; Manifold prices a 2026 runoff at ~27%.

base_rates.text: Recent Georgia top-of-ballot federal races decided inside ~3 points (Biden +0.24, Ossoff +1.2, Warnock +1.6, Warnock +0.9/runoff +2.8, Trump +2.2). Structurally a coin-flip top line — the strongest argument the mid-year lead compresses.
Kalshi SENATEGA-26 last price on an Ossoff/Democratic win (Collins ~16c), matched by Polymarket ~85% — the deepest exact-question market anchor, pulled 2026-07-03.

Trump-endorsed MAGA Senate nominees vs. Democratic swing-state holds in 2022 (Walker/Oz/Masters/Bolduc). A candidate-quality caution for Collins — but all four ran in a Democrat-favorable year, unlike 2026.

Democratic incumbents held Trump-won states in the nearest analog midterm, 2018 (~43%). A floor, not the central estimate, since 2018 favored Democrats while a Republican-president midterm penalty cuts toward Ossoff.
House midterms since 1938 in which the president's party lost ground (~91%). A structural out-party tailwind for Democrats in a 2026 Republican-president midterm.
Senate incumbent reelection floor (2022: 35/35; 2018 ~83%; 2014 ~79%). Favors the incumbent to win — but this is a win-rate, not a comfortable-margin rate, consistent with a narrow hold.
Thin play-money Manifold price on a December runoff; two of the last three competitive Georgia Senate cycles went to one. Discounted for a weaker 2026 third-party field to a 10-18% runoff branch.

triggers: Two consecutive post-Labor-Day live-caller likely-voter (not registered-voter) polls showing Ossoff +8 or more — shifts mass to the comfortable-win scenario.
The polling average tightening inside D+2, or two likely-voter polls showing Collins within 2 or ahead — shifts mass toward Collins and the runoff.
October early-vote composition showing depressed Black or under-30 turnout share vs. 2020/2022 — the single most decisive turnout signal for reversion to Georgia's structural margin.
Kalshi's Collins leg (OI ~171k) moving above 20c or below 12c — a real-money re-pricing that re-weights every scenario.
A macro shock (CPI re-acceleration or recession signal) bringing Ossoff's inflation-voter edge below +10 from the current +21 — the largest single driver-reversal, toward Collins.
A credible Libertarian qualifying for the Georgia ballot and polling 2%+ with both majors under 48% — mechanically raises the runoff branch.
Collins closing the cash gap below ~3:1 via national transfers (lifts Collins), or a Walker-2022-magnitude Collins scandal (collapses him and vindicates the 0-of-4 MAGA-nominee anchor).
A candidate exit, indictment, or health event — activates the tail scenario and invalidates the incumbency reference class for that nominee.

method_note: Anchored on the deepest exact-question market — Kalshi near 85c on an Ossoff win, backed by Polymarket (~85%) and a thin Manifold market (~74%), pulled July 3, 2026. Because Georgia's six-of-six recent sub-three-point finishes say the mid-year lead overstates the result, win probability splits by margin: total Ossoff-win mass near 0.78, the December runoff (~14%) carved out, the rest split narrow vs. comfortable. Collins nudged above 15% to 18-30%. Horizon: through November 3, 2026.
honesty_note: The modal call — a narrow Ossoff win at 44-54% — sits near a coin flip and is more likely to NOT land exactly as described than to land: pool the runoff, comfortable-win, Collins, and shock branches and there is close to an even chance the result takes a different shape. Treat this as a lean with a live Republican path and a real runoff tail, not a settled outcome.
